title: Secure Collaborative Model Training with Dynamic Federated Learning in Multi-Domain Environments
problem: Airlines cannot easily combine fleet data for predictive maintenance due to data ownership concerns including privacy, intellectual property protection, and regulatory compliance. Organizations need a way to collaboratively train ML models while maintaining individual data control.
motivation: Collaborative analysis of fleet data could enable early detection of engine failures through improved predictive maintenance algorithms, enhancing aviation safety and efficiency.
method: The approach uses Federated Learning combined with microservices architecture to enable collaborative ML model training. Each airline maintains local data control while participating in global model training using the NASA Turbofan Jet Engine Dataset (N-CMAPSS). Local model updates are aggregated into a global model without centralizing sensitive data.
key_novelty: Applying federated learning with microservices architecture to enable privacy-preserving collaborative predictive maintenance model training across multiple airlines while preserving data ownership.
contributions: Federated learning methodology for privacy-preserving collaborative ML in aviation
Microservices-based architecture for coordinating multi-domain federated training
Demonstration using N-CMAPSS dataset for collaborative predictive maintenance
Solution addressing data privacy, intellectual property, and regulatory compliance barriers
